note.headline: Tech slide continues as fear rises; trend, fear and breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: Both SPY and QQQ are in downtrends, below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is 'elevated' and rose on the day, and only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. All three readings point the same way.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term and swing buying, until QQQ closes above 682.54, its 200-day average and the market gate.
summary.act_at: QQQ 682.54 (market gate, above). QQQ 608.45 and SPY 689.81 (1-month lows, below).

note.happening: On Nov 25, SPY closed at 716.7, down 0.29% on the day, 1.85% over 5 days and 7.2% over 20 days. QQQ fell more: it closed at 633.93, down 0.65% on the day, 3.88% over 5 days and 12.63% over 20 days. Both peaked for the month on Oct 28, at 772.31 for SPY and 725.61 for QQQ. Both set their 1-month lows on Nov 20, at 689.81 for SPY and 608.45 for QQQ. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. The VIX fear gauge closed at 28.29, up from 26.36. DATA reports no news since the last note.
note.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50- and 200-day averages, which DATA classifies as a downtrend. QQQ is 7.7% below its 200-day average and 11.5% below its 50-day. SPY is 2.0% below its 200-day and 5.7% below its 50-day. So tech is weaker than the broad market. Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, which means the selling is broad and not limited to a few large names. Taken together, the readings agree: prices are falling, fear is near the top of its yearly range, and few stocks are holding up. Both indices still sit above their Nov 20 lows (QQQ 4.0% above, SPY 3.8% above), so that low is holding for now.

worth.text: This is a price-trend note, not a valuation. DATA contains no earnings or valuation inputs, so no fair-value range is given.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indices are still above their Nov 20 1-month lows (QQQ 608.45, SPY 689.81), so the recent low is holding.
SPY is only 2.0% below its 200-day average of 730.77, much closer to repairing its long-term trend than QQQ.
bear: QQQ is down 12.63% over 20 days and 7.7% below its 200-day average, so the market gate at 682.54 is still far away.
Fear rose on the day, with VIX at 28.29 against 26.36 the day before. That is close to the 'high' band that starts at 30.
Breadth of 8% means almost no stocks are in short-term uptrends, so setups keep failing the pipeline's market check.

QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

swing.why: QQQ is 11.5% below its 50-day average of 707.02. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check, and the 0.65% drop on Nov 25 moved QQQ further away from it.

The nearest levels are SPY 730.77 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.54 above and 608.45 below. The 50- and 200-day averages move every day, while the 1-month highs and lows are fixed past prices.

A close below the 1-month lows, QQQ 608.45 or SPY 689.81, would mean the decline is continuing and would reinforce standing aside. A VIX move into the 30+ 'high' band would point the same way.

note.headline: Tesla holds 380.14 under resistance; margins and cash flow weak, still avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have gone flat and its margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the share price sits near the top of its own 5-year valuation range.
summary.decision: Long-term avoid; swing wait, because the price is stuck in a range just under heavy resistance.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 after the 2027-01-27 report; swing only above 404.4 or on a hold at 363.86–368.76

note.happening: Tesla fell 1.18% to 380.14. That leaves it just under a resistance zone at 380.15–389.95, where sellers have stepped in 9 times, and all three moving averages (20, 50 and 200 days) are flat. No news has been reported since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Several numbers point to the business itself getting weaker. Sales in the latest quarter changed -0.17% from a year earlier, after 15.78% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (the profit kept from each sales dollar before interest and tax) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) dropped to 3.3B over the last 12 months, from 6.8B. Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which would put margins under more pressure. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. Those are changes to demand, margins and cash. What is not at risk is the balance sheet: net cash is 37.5B and total liquidity is 45.4B, so funding is not a concern. The internal macro view of a tech downtrend with elevated fear only affects sentiment, not the business. Segment data is not available, so this note cannot say which product lines are driving the slowdown.

worth.text: The methods disagree badly, and the gap comes down to growth. A discounted cash flow (DCF) model values a company from the cash it is expected to produce. Starting from trailing free cash flow of 3.3B and a 9.9% discount rate, it gives 20.17 (bear), 24.93 (base) and 45.0 (bull). Even if growth starts at 30%, the value is 45.37. The filings-based risk check says today's price needs about 51% a year growth, while the company has delivered 3% a year over 3 years and 8% over the last 12 months. On Tesla's own history, the price-to-sales ratio (price divided by sales per share) gives 203.8 at its 20th percentile, 293.94 at the middle and 399.81 at its 80th percentile. Today's price-to-sales of 14.5 sits at the 73rd percentile of its 5-year range, and the trailing price-to-earnings ratio is 418.3. If operating margin falls to 2%, the DCF value is 27.91. My range uses the lower half of Tesla's own valuation history, because the cash-flow models cannot reach today's price under any growth they test.
worth.key_assumption: With flat quarterly sales and operating margin down to 3.35%, the market will value Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top.

bull: The balance sheet is very strong: net cash is 37.5B and liquidity is 45.4B, which leaves room to keep investing through a slow patch.
Analysts' next-year EPS growth figure is 25%, and the DCF bull case using the highest growth input is 45.0, well above the base of 24.93.
Sales over the last 12 months still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and R&D spending is 8.56% of revenue, which keeps new products funded.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B, and the DCF base value is 24.93 against a price of 380.14.
Operating margin dropped to 3.35% from 4.74%, and inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which raises the risk of price cuts.
The valuation is stretched: trailing price-to-earnings is 418.3 and price-to-sales of 14.5 sits at the 73rd percentile of its own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is close to the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.93, so value offers no support at this price.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.86–368.76), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it points to the next zone at 349.24–354.14.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine at this price only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales growth, margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all weakening while the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The business grade is D and the internal committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The price sits just under resistance at 380.15–389.95 (9 touches), the averages are flat and the trend is a range, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or until a pullback holds at 363.86–368.76.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price an 11.5% move by 2026-12-18 and a 20.2% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report, and recent actual swings (72.9) have been bigger than what options imply (56.1).

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth from a year earlier back above 0%.
Trailing free cash flow recovers toward 6.8B from 3.3B, which would lift the cash base the DCF starts from.
A close above 404.4, the top of the second resistance zone, would end the range and change the swing call from wait.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid long-term and wait on the swing; with no new news, the close of 380.14 just under the 380.15–389.95 resistance zone confirmed it.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA holds 149.30 support as shipment halt and governance worries are reported

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is still a grade A business. It is priced for less growth than its cash-flow models assume, but its margin is at a peak and new risks to demand and governance are reported.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, not add; swing wait until the downtrend breaks.
summary.act_at: Hold above 147.13; buy at 117.15; trim near 226.93

note.happening: The stock closed at 149.30, down 3.91% on the day. It sits inside the 147.13–150.47 price zone, in a downtrend below its falling 20-day (172.48) and 50-day (203.65) averages. Since that close, NVIDIA was reported to have halted chip shipments to south-east Asia, Jensen Huang's return as CEO was reported, and S&P was reported (unconfirmed) to be considering a credit downgrade over governance and 'key man' risk.
note.business: The business numbers are still very strong. Quarterly sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, faster than the 73.21% two quarters ago. The operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and trailing free cash flow reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. Two of today's items could change the business itself. First, the reported halt of shipments to south-east Asia touches demand: a region that stops buying means lost sales, though our data has no segment split to size it. Second, unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. The return of the founder as CEO, the opinion columns and the reported S&P warning change sentiment and governance, not demand. A credit rating cut would raise the cost of borrowing (general knowledge), but NVIDIA has 23.2B of net cash and 56.6B of liquidity, so its cash position is not at risk. The real exposure is the margin: 65% is the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, and the filings note that peaks like this usually fade.

worth.text: At 149.30 the stock trades at 18.8 times trailing earnings, 15.4 times this year's estimate and 9.0 times next year's. Its price-to-sales of 11.9 is below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4th percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow models give 194.8 (bear), 226.93 (base) and 270.18 (bull), and its own sales-multiple history gives 217.35–411.04. So every method lands above today's price. What explains the gap is the starting growth rate. The price implies free cash flow growth starting near 18.9%, while the models cap starting growth at 30%. At 20% starting growth the value is 155.88, close to the price. At 10% it is 105.42. The models also keep today's peak margin. If the operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 117.15. At 32% it drops to 78.42. So the stock looks cheap only if the margin holds.
worth.key_assumption: The operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, and free cash flow growth starts above the 18.9% the price implies.

bull: Analysts raised next-year EPS estimates by 27.7% over 90 days, to 16.61, which puts the stock at 9.0 times next year's earnings.
Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters ago, with free cash flow of 127.0B over the last 12 months.
Price-to-sales of 11.9 is below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4th percentile of its own 5-year history.
bear: The 65.21% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range. A fade to 48% cuts model value to 117.15, below today's 149.30.
Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which can signal pulled-forward sales or customers paying slowly.
Insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans, and the price is in a downtrend below its 50-day average of 203.65.

levels.what: Bottom of the zone the price sits in (147.13–150.47). A close below it moves the call to wait, with the next support at 122.83–126.17.
Model value if the operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 117.15, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
Base-case cash-flow value. Trim near it, because at that price the full peak margin and 30% starting growth would be priced in.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. The price looks cheap only if a peak margin holds, and the reported shipment halt and slow customer payments are unresolved. So the call is hold, not add.

swing.why: The trend is down, with lower highs and lower lows. A typical day's range of 13.38 would break through any tight stop under 147.13, and the nearest support below is 122.83–126.17. No trade until the price closes above 171.33, the top of the resistance zone with 4 touches.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date. The latest filing covers the quarter to 2026-07-26, and analysts expect EPS of 2.88 on 130.8B of revenue for this quarter. The reported news came after the 149.30 close, so the next session's price reaction to it sets the timing more than any calendar date.

change_mind: A close below 147.13 moves the long-term call to wait, with the next support at 122.83–126.17.

If the next filing shows the operating margin falling back toward 58.09%, or unpaid bills again growing faster than sales, the case shifts toward the 117.15 margin-fade value and the hold becomes avoid above that level.
A close above 171.33 would end the swing wait. A next-year EPS estimate falling back below 15.91 (the level 30 days ago) would weaken the bull case.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: hold. The price staying at 149.30, inside the 147.13–150.47 zone, confirmed it, while the reported south-east Asia shipment halt adds demand risk that argues against adding; the margin-fade buy level is now 117.15 (data updated from 116.97).
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD holds just above support at 406.03, still priced well above fair value

summary.thesis: AMD's business is growing fast and getting more profitable, but at 406.03 the price already assumes much more growth than any valuation method supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price; swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Buy case starts at 333.38; swing only after a close above 451.0

note.happening: AMD fell 1.75% to 406.03, just above a support zone at 391.92–403.54, in a confirmed downtrend: the 20-day average of 489.22 is falling and the price is below the 50-day (548.35) and 200-day (432.96) averages. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: These are real changes to the business. Quarterly revenue grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) roughly doubled to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after investment) rose to 7.1B from 5.4B, and AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so the balance sheet is not at risk. Analysts raised next-year earnings estimates by 11.3% in 30 days. The filings show two risks to the business. Inventory is up 57% while sales are up 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. Also, the 18% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that tend to fade. The price drop itself changes only sentiment: the tech market is in a downtrend and fear is elevated. Options traders hold 2.61 puts (bets on a fall) for every call, which also points to fear rather than a change in the business.

worth.text: Every method puts fair value below the price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 147.69 to 225.08 per share, with 189.77 in the middle. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. To justify 406.03, free cash flow would need to start growing at 51.7% a year, while the model caps starting growth at 30%, which gives 190.08. The gap comes from analysts' 118% jump in next-year EPS: the price assumes that pace lasts, and the models assume it fades. On the market's own measures, the stock trades at 88.5 times trailing earnings but only 23.0 times next year's estimate. Its price-to-sales of 14.7 compares with a peer median of 12.0 and sits at the 88th percentile of its own 5-year range. If operating margin slips back to 13%, the model's value drops to 100.16.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies 51.7% a year against a 30% cap, so it holds up only if next-year EPS growth of 118% keeps going.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly revenue growth rose to 44.68% from 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability is rising: operating margin went to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow grew to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Estimates keep going up: next-year EPS of 17.64 was raised 11.3% in 30 days, which brings the forward P/E down to 23.0.
bear: The price of 406.03 is above every fair-value method, whose top is 333.38.
Inventory is up 57% against a 45% rise in sales, which could force price cuts and lower margins.
If operating margin falls back to 13%, the model's value drops to 100.16, and the stock already costs 14.7 times sales against a peer median of 12.0.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 391.92–403.54 support zone. A close below it points to the next zone at 347.18–358.8, which is still above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, from AMD's own price-to-sales history. The value case for buying starts here.

change_mind: A close below 391.92 would break support and open the 347.18–358.8 zone; at 333.38 or lower, the long-term case moves to buy.
A close above 451.0, together with a 2027-02-02 report at or above the 3.3 EPS estimate, would end the swing no-trade stance.
Inventory growth falling back below sales growth (now 57% vs 45%) while operating margin holds near 17.72% would make the high-growth case easier to defend.

note.headline: Amazon at 244.43 after 3.12% drop; still waiting for 238.65 before buying

summary.thesis: Amazon still grows sales and margins, but it is burning cash, its growth is slowing, and at 244.43 the price sits above the middle of its own value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 238.65. Swing: no trade while the stock is in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Buy at 238.65, add at 226.88, no buying above 265.96

note.happening: Amazon fell 3.12% to 244.43. That puts it below its 200-day average of 245.78 and well below its 20-day (257.19) and 50-day (255.12) averages, so the trend is down. News outlets reported that Amazon lost another attempt to avoid handling more recall notices, and that Korean beauty brands are topping Amazon bestseller lists ahead of Black Friday. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-04.
note.business: Three things change the business. First, growth is slowing: sales in the latest quarter grew 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Second, margins are better: operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. The filings note that 13% is the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. Third, cash is the main problem. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business and its equipment) was -46.9B over the last 12 months, against 10.6B a year before. Debt of 180.9B is larger than cash of 55.8B, so net cash is -66.7B. Liquidity of 114.2B means there is no near-term funding strain. The filings also flag that unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Both news items affect sentiment or governance, not demand. The recall ruling is a compliance burden, and the bestseller report is a small, positive sign of holiday traffic. At risk: cash generation and the pace of growth. Not at risk: the scale of revenue (797.5B over 12 months, up from 691.3B) or the company's ability to pay its bills. Segment data is not available, so the source of the cash burn cannot be pinned down here.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value (a method that values a company on its future cash) because free cash flow is negative. That leaves the stock's own history of price-to-sales, meaning what investors have paid for each dollar of sales. On that measure, fair value runs from 187.93 (20th percentile) through 238.65 (middle) to 265.96 (80th percentile). At 244.43 the price is above the middle. Price-to-sales is 3.3, at the 60th percentile of its own 5 years and far below the peer median of 6.5. That gap is what the bull case relies on. On earnings, the stock trades at 19.8 times trailing earnings and 19.1 times this year's estimate. It trades at 22.9 times next year's estimate because analysts expect earnings per share to dip to 10.67 from 12.8. The filings estimate that today's price implies about 33% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. So the price already assumes much more than the business has shown.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.5.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now keeps more profit.
Price-to-sales of 3.3 is far below the peer median of 6.5, and the growth-adjusted ratio against peers is 0.58, which means the stock is cheaper than peers even after allowing for growth.
Analysts expect next-year revenue of 959.6B, against 797.5B over the last 12 months, and their next-year EPS estimate rose 1.4% over 30 days.
bear: Free cash flow swung to -46.9B from 10.6B a year earlier, and net cash is -66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while the price implies about 33% a year growth.
Analysts expect earnings per share to fall to 10.67 next year from 12.8 this year, and the next-quarter estimate was cut 3.4% over 90 days.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history value range. It sits inside the 233.59–238.97 support zone, where buyers have stepped in 3 times before. This is the main buy level.
The bottom of the deeper 226.88–232.99 support zone (4 touches). This is the level to add, if the first buy fills and the zone holds.
The top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: At 244.43 the price is still above the 238.65 middle of its value range. The cash burn and slowing growth are unresolved, the business grade is D, and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (257.19), 50-day (255.12) and 200-day (245.78) averages, and its typical daily move is 10.45. No trade unless the price holds the 233.59–238.97 support zone or closes above 258.08, the top of a resistance zone that has turned the price back 7 times.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-04 report is the next real test. Options expiring 2027-02-19, after that report, price in a move of about 16.3%, against 8.5% for 2026-12-18, so any buy before the report starts at 238.65 and no higher.

If the 2027-02-04 report shows 12-month free cash flow improving from -46.9B while quarterly sales growth holds at or above 12.09%, the long-term case would move from wait toward buy.
A close below 226.88, the bottom of the deeper support zone, would remove the add level and point toward the 187.93 low of the value range.

note.headline: Microsoft holds 489.93 above support; no new news, hold and swing plan unchanged

summary.thesis: The business is growing faster and more profitably, but free cash flow is shrinking and the price already assumes a lot.
summary.decision: Long-term hold with an add level at 474.82; swing entry stays at 485.06 with a 475.34 stop and a 503.99 target.

note.happening: Microsoft closed at 489.93, down 1.25% on the day. That puts it in today's price zone of 485.58–490.27, just above the 475.34–485.06 support zone. There is no new news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Demand is improving. Quarterly sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts raised next year's earnings-per-share estimate to 24.2 from 23.68 a month ago. The weak spot is cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B. The filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, against 51¢ three years ago. In plain words, heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 29.0B and liquidity is 64.5B. Yesterday's note cited a reported outage. Nothing in DATA shows it touching sales or margins, so it counts as sentiment, not business. The four new risk headings in the annual report are a governance item to read, not a change to the numbers.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model (DCF), which values the company on the free cash it can produce in future, gives 183.71 to 295.41 with a base of 222.45. That is far below the price. To justify 489.93 on cash flow, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 39.3% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even that gives only 350.66. Against its own history the picture is different. Valued on price-to-sales (company value divided by yearly sales) at its usual 5-year levels, the stock is worth 474.82 to 591.77, with a midpoint of 534.4. The gap between the methods comes from one assumption: whether the 60.0B of trailing free cash flow is a temporary dip caused by heavy spending, or the new normal. On earnings it costs 25.6 times trailing profit and 20.2 times next year's estimate. Against peers it is expensive: 10.5 times sales versus a peer median of 3.7.
